_meta.subject: Running costs of owning a Cessna 172S Skyhawk in the United States
_meta.conventions: sourceType 'primary' = the maker's or authority's own page or document; 'secondary' = press, broker, shop or forum. confirmed = true only where the figure was read directly on the cited page or document during this research; false where it came only from a search-engine summary or could not be opened. Figures not published are null with a note. Derived figures say how they were derived.
notes: Textron's current Skyhawk spec page gives no fuel-burn figure; the burn below comes from the 172S Nav III Information Manual (a copy of the POH/AFM), Section 1 and Figure 5-8.

Lycoming SI 1009 is now at revision BF (July 20, 2026). BF added a separate 'Factory New/Rebuilt' TBO column: 2600 hours for the IO-360-L2A on its first run after a factory-new or factory-rebuilt engine, 2000 hours after any overhaul.
The FAA survey figure for hours flown is the average of all active piston singles, including flight schools. The personal-use figure is derived from two FAA tables and is labeled as such.

fuelBurn.aircraft: Cessna 172S (Nav III / G1000), Lycoming IO-360-L2A, 180 hp
fuelBurn.gphAt75PctCruiseNote: Derived: Information Manual Section 4 gives 124 KTAS at 12.2 NMPG at 75% power, 8000 ft (124 / 12.2 = 10.16 gph). Figure 5-8 cruise table at 8000 ft, standard temperature, recommended lean: 2650 RPM = 72% MCP, 122 KTAS, 9.9 gph; 2700 RPM = 77% MCP, 124 KTAS, 10.4 gph. At 4000 ft, 2550 RPM = 73% MCP, 9.9 gph. So a 75% cruise burns about 10 to 10.4 gph by the book.
fuelBurn.tableConditions: 2550 lb, recommended lean mixture, standard temperature, speed fairings installed

source.title: Cessna Model 172S Nav III GFC 700 AFCS Information Manual (Original Issue, 20 December 2007), Section 1 Performance - Specifications, Section 4 Cruise, Section 5 Figure 5-8 Cruise Performance
source.note: Cessna's own document, hosted by a flight school. The manual itself says it is not kept current and is not a substitute for the aircraft's POH/AFM.

corroboration.value: 9.9 gph at 75% power, best economy; 124 kt
corroboration.title: AOPA Aircraft Guide: Cessna 172S

corroboration.value: Textron spec page: max cruise 124 ktas, range 640 nm, usable fuel 53 gal, IO-360-L2A 180 hp; no fuel-burn figure published
corroboration.title: Cessna Skyhawk specifications (Textron Aviation)

nationalAverage.note: AirNav's own report, all FBOs reporting 100LL, not split into full or self service.

nationalAverageFullServiceGlobalAir.note: GlobalAir full-service average, reported by AVweb. GlobalAir's own regional page returned 403. Same article: AirNav then at $7.22 across 3,583 FBOs; Alaska highest at $11.61, Central lowest at $7.00 (GlobalAir).

regional.note: AirNav region; FAA Western-Pacific covers California, Nevada, Arizona and Hawaii. Used as the closest published proxy for California.
FAA Eastern region includes New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Delaware, Maryland, Virginia, West Virginia and DC.

avgas.californiaOnlyNote: No California-only statewide average was found published; AirNav and GlobalAir publish by FAA region. Use Western-Pacific ($7.74) or a specific airport's posted price.
avgas.northeastNote: 'Northeast' is not an AirNav region. New England ($7.88) and Eastern ($7.60) together cover it; the New York City area sits in the Eastern region, Connecticut in New England.

fuelCostPerHourAt75Pct.note: Derived: 10.2 gph x the AirNav averages above. Excludes oil.

engine.tboNotes: SI 1009BF Table 1 lists IO-360-L2A: Factory New/Rebuilt 2600 hours (no note); Overhaul 2000 hours, Notes 11, 15, 16. Note 11: add 200 hours for 'frequent' service (at least 120 hours in every rolling 90 days, no 30-day period under 20 hours) - a private owner will not qualify. Note 15: add 200 hours for a Lycoming factory overhaul, or a field overhaul meeting all the listed conditions (genuine Lycoming parts only, among others). Note 16: Notes 11 and 15 together can add 400 hours. All engines to be overhauled within 12 calendar years of entering service or last overhaul; under Part 91 a qualified mechanic may allow that to be exceeded after an Appendix D-based examination repeated annually.

tboSource.title: Lycoming Service Instruction No. 1009BF, Time Between Overhaul (TBO) Schedules

overhaulCost.note: Quoted for Lycoming four-cylinder IO-320/IO-360 engines as a group, not specifically the -L2A. Removal, reinstallation, propeller work and accessories are extra.

source.title: Lycoming IO-Series Engine Overhaul Cost and Time to Expect (Flying411)

reservePerHour.fieldOverhaulBasis: Derived: midpoint major-shop field overhaul $43,000 + midpoint removal/reinstall $7,500 = $50,500 / 2000 h = $25.25, rounded to $25.
reservePerHour.factoryRebuildBasis: Derived: ($64,000 + $7,500 removal/reinstall) / 2600 h (first-run TBO for a factory-rebuilt engine under SI 1009BF) = $27.50. Excludes the core charge, which is refunded when an acceptable core is returned.
reservePerHour.calendarLimitNote: At the private-owner rate of about 60 hours a year, 2000 hours takes over 30 years, so the 12-year calendar TBO usually governs unless a mechanic extends it. Over 12 years at 63 h/yr (756 h), a $50,500 overhaul works out to about $67 per hour - the realistic reserve for a low-use private owner who overhauls on the calendar.

aopaMethod.text: AOPA divides the overhaul cost by TBO; its dated example is a $17,000 overhaul / 2000 h = $8.50 per hour.
aopaMethod.note: Method only; the $17,000 figure is long out of date.

annual.inspectionFlatRateNote: One shop's published flat rate for a 'Late Model 172' (the 172R/172S): 20 labor hours for $1,800 ($90/h). Older 172s: 18 h, $1,620. Findings and parts are extra.

source.title: Lore Aviation Services - Inspection Price Sheet
source.note: The page carries a 2026 copyright notice but no date for the prices, and no location.

otherFigures.value: About $1,700 for the inspection; findings extra
otherFigures.title: What Does a 172 Annual Cost These Days? (Plane & Pilot, Amy Wilder)

otherFigures.value: Inspection fee $1,500-$2,200 for a well-kept 172 in 2026; total annual with findings $2,500-$4,500 for a healthy airplane; $8,000-$12,000 for one with deferred maintenance
otherFigures.title: Aircraft Annual Inspection Cost in 2026: Owner Guide (e3 Aviation Association)
otherFigures.note: From the search-engine summary only; the article body did not load when fetched.

otherFigures.value: One shop: Cessna 170/172/175, 18 hours, $2,124 flat rate
otherFigures.title: Flat Rate Annual Inspection (WCS Aviation)

annual.typicalTotalNote: Secondary and not confirmed on the page; see e3 Aviation Association above. Use for a healthy airplane only.

hoursFlown.faaAllUsesNote: FAA Table 2.1 (2024): 1-engine 4+ seats, 98,291 active aircraft, 12,629,343 hours, average 128.5; all piston singles 114.9 (Table 1.5 gives 114.5 for 2023). These include flight-school, rental and business flying, so they overstate a private owner's use.

personalUseDerived.basis: Derived: Table 3.2 personal-use hours (1-engine 4+ seats: 4,725,980; all 1-engine: 5,804,081) / Table 3.1 active aircraft whose primary use is personal (75,052; 99,439). Approximate, because Table 3.2 counts hours by actual use while Table 3.1 counts aircraft by primary use.

source.title: FAA General Aviation and Part 135 Activity Survey, CY 2024 - Chapter 1 (Table 1.5), Chapter 2 (Table 2.1), Chapter 3 (Tables 3.1, 3.2)

hoursFlown.aopaOrGamaNote: No AOPA or GAMA survey of private-owner hours was found published. AOPA's operating-cost guide uses 100 h/yr only as a worked example; a 2026 ownership-cost article (Jaken Aviation) assumes 75 h/yr. Neither is survey data.

hangars.hwdNote: Hayward Executive Airport (HWD) fees are already on file and are not repeated here.

nearNewYorkCity.airport: Waterbury-Oxford Airport (KOXC), Oxford, Connecticut - about 65 miles from Manhattan
nearNewYorkCity.terms: License agreement required; due monthly in advance on the 1st; not prorated; no daily rate; 5 days' notice to terminate before month end; where the FBO handles the aircraft, FBO rates apply. Same rate at Hartford-Brainard (KHFD) and Groton-New London (KGON). Windham and Danielson: $55 unpaved / $65 paved single engine.
nearNewYorkCity.hangarNote: The CAA sheet publishes no hangar rate.

source.title: General Aviation Airports Rates and Charges - July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027 (Connecticut Airport Authority)

nearNewYorkCity.airport: Westchester County Airport (HPN), White Plains, New York
nearNewYorkCity.operator: Million Air (FBO; county-owned airport) - an FBO rate, not a municipal one
nearNewYorkCity.terms: Was $375/month for about ten years; $600 from October 2025, rising $50 a quarter to $800 in October 2026, then indexed to local CPI. AOPA contested it.

source.title: AOPA contests fee increase at Westchester County Airport

nearNewYorkCity.airport: Republic Airport (FRG), East Farmingdale, New York
nearNewYorkCity.operator: New York State Department of Transportation
nearNewYorkCity.note: No current NYSDOT rate schedule is published online. The last published figure is the 2008 NYSDOT release raising 'plane parking fees' from $105 to $140 for single-engine planes (the release does not say per month). Too old to use as current. Based tiedowns and T-hangars are now leased through the FBOs.

source.title: NYSDOT Approves New Rates and Charges for Republic Airport (press release)

nearNewYorkCity.note: $170 with electric outlet. FBO rate, not a city rate; undated.

source.title: Tie-Down Rentals Available, Danbury Municipal Airport (Business Aircraft Center)

insurance.assumptions: Personal use, hull $80,000-$150,000, $1,000,000 smooth liability, pilot with 250+ total hours, clean history, hangared.
insurance.note: Published by an insurance broker; figures are the broker's own ranges, not filed rates. A new 172S (list price $419,620 per AOPA's guide) at 0.9-1.3% of hull would run about $3,800-$5,500 for hull alone.

source.title: Airplane Insurance Cost for a Cessna 172 in 2026 - Real Numbers (BWI Fly)

uncertain: Fuel burn at exactly 75% is not a single POH number: the Information Manual gives 124 KTAS at 12.2 NMPG (about 10.2 gph); the Figure 5-8 table brackets 75% between 9.9 and 10.4 gph. AOPA quotes 9.9 gph.
AirNav ($7.25, 29 Sep 2026) and GlobalAir ($7.69 full-service, about 25 Sep 2026) differ because AirNav averages all posted 100LL prices while GlobalAir's is full-service only.
No California-only or 'Northeast' avgas average is published; FAA-region averages stand in.
Overhaul prices are for Lycoming four-cylinder IO-320/IO-360 engines as a group, not quoted for the IO-360-L2A alone.
Engine reserve per hour is derived, and for a low-use owner the 12-year calendar TBO, not the 2000-hour limit, usually decides when the overhaul comes.
Personal-use hours per aircraft (63.0 for 4+ seat singles) is derived from two FAA tables that count use differently; treat as approximate.
The annual-inspection flat rate ($1,800) is one shop's price sheet with no date or location; the $2,500-$4,500 total-with-findings range was not confirmed on its page.
Republic Airport (FRG) has no current published NYSDOT tiedown rate; the only published figure dates from 2008.
Westchester (HPN) and Danbury (DXR) rates are FBO rates, not municipal ones; the Danbury figure was not confirmed on its page.
Insurance ranges come from a broker's marketing article, not from filed rates or an industry survey.
